independent_artefacts_refetched.note: Papers/ is untracked and was EMPTY in this worktree, so items (1)-(3) could not be measured from anything already on disk. That turns items (1) and (2) from a TRANSCRIPTION CHECK into a MEASUREMENT.

item_2_T4_first_conjunct_and_negative_co.radii_polynomial_convention: The paper's (4.33)/(4.34) -- read by me from the re-fetched PDF at pdftotext line 2626-2632 -- are r_min = [1-(Z0+Z1) - sqrt((1-(Z0+Z1))^2 - 2*Y0*Z2)] / Z2 and r_max = [1-(Z0+Z1)] / Z2. r_max is the VALIDITY BOUND, not the larger root. My pre-registered guess (the textbook 1/2-free quadratic, r_max = larger root) was WRONG and is recorded here as MY error, not the record's: under the paper's own (4.33)/(4.34) both radii reproduce bit-for-bit.

zgliczynski.nuance: The NAME appears exactly once, as bibliography item [48]. undercut_2.banked_deciding_sentence: our results, depending on numerical approximations, do not guarantee that the Navier-Stokes solutions exhibit chaotic behaviour in the sense of Devaney
undercut_2.wall_bc_sentence_i_read_myself: The boundary conditions at the inner and outer cylinder walls r = r_i and r = r_o are v = R_i theta-hat and v = R_o theta-hat. Periodicity is enforced to the rest of boundaries of the parallelogram domain. (p.4, sec 2)
undercut_2.nuance: The paper never uses the literal phrase 'no-slip' (0 occurrences). What it states is a MOVING-WALL DIRICHLET condition v = R_i theta-hat / R_o theta-hat at r = r_i, r_o -- the no-slip condition on a rotating cylinder -- with periodicity only 'to the rest of boundaries'. So the domain is NOT a pure periodic cell, which is the substance of the claim; 'no-slip walls, not periodicity' is a compression of the paper's own words.

The gate's wording makes the wall BC the ground ('carries no-slip walls, not periodicity, SO ... over-counts by one'). Both facts are in the record and both reproduce; the CAUSAL LINK differs between the gate's wording and the record's. REPORTED, NOT RECONCILED.
